s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic wound with progressive pain and skin irritation in the sacral area
salient_findings: Chronic superficial sacral wound present for approximately 2 years
Progressively worsening sacral pain and local skin irritation
Presence of a small superior sinus tract with mild serous discharge
key_facts: Ischemic heart disease status post coronary artery bypass grafting
Medications include aspirin, rosuvastatin, valsartan, and topical corticosteroids
Afebrile and systemically well on examination
Coccygectomy scar slightly indurated and surrounded by excoriated skin
Presence of plaques and focal ulceration in the upper natal cleft
Lesion located more than 5 cm from the anal verge
No exophytic mass, no underlying abscess cavity, and no palpable inguinal lymphadenopathy

shortlist.label: Pilonidal sinus
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic superficial sacral wound with sinus tract and location in the natal cleft

shortlist.label: Chronic hidradenitis suppurativa
shortlist.why_kept: History of inverse psoriasis and presence of plaques and focal ulceration in the upper natal cleft

shortlist.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Progressively worsening sacral pain and local skin irritation with ulceration

shortlist.label: Sacral pressure ulcer
shortlist.why_kept: Location of the lesion more than 5 cm from the anal verge and presence of excoriated skin

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of multiple cutaneous nonmelanoma skin cancers and presence of a chronic wound

raw.rationale: The presence of a chronic superficial sacral wound with progressively worsening sacral pain, local skin irritation, and the absence of purulent discharge or altered bowel habits, along with a history of inverse psoriasis and the appearance of plaques and focal ulceration, are more consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum, especially given the lack of evidence supporting other conditions like pilonidal sinus or squamous cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Pilonidal sinus
rejected.why: Typically presents with a sinus tract and often purulent discharge, which is not the primary presentation here.

rejected.label: Chronic hidradenitis suppurativa
rejected.why: Usually involves apocrine gland-bearing areas and is characterized by recurrent, painful abscesses and nodules, not primarily a superficial wound.

rejected.label: Sacral pressure ulcer
rejected.why: Would be expected in areas of pressure, especially in immobilized patients, and does not fully account for the chronicity and specific characteristics of the wound.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Magnetic resonance imaging showed no invasion of underlying structures and no visible metastases, making this less likely without further diagnostic evidence like a biopsy.
